1.why: All MFA endpoints use authenticatedSession/requireAuth, which binds the HttpOnly session to account.id and rejects mismatched or missing ownership.

2.why: OTP/recovery verification uses the single account secret from the authenticated session only; codes are not accepted across arbitrary users and no user-id parameter selects another account.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets mfaEnabled and does not invalidate or re-check other existing authenticated sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: encryptedSecret and encryptedRecoveryCodes are stored via AES-256-GCM encrypt(), not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, and recovery codes are produced with node:crypto randomBytes.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly Secure cookie; code does not write secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, and recovery code with strict validators and rejects unexpected JSON bodies including accountId/userId.

8.why: Client inserts dynamic values with textContent/createTextNode and CSP nonce disables inline script injection; API responses are JSON.

9.why: No redirect handling or internal allow-list exists anywhere in the server or client code.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: cookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Server errors are generic without stack traces and tokens are not in URLs, but the UI deliberately logs manual secret, test OTP, and recovery codes into the on-page log output.

13.why: TOTP accepts a counter only once via acceptedCounter and is time-windowed; recovery codes are removed on use and carry expiresAt.

14.why: failed()/locked() lock the account after MAX_FAILURES (5) for LOCKOUT (10 minutes) on verify and recovery verify.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the preauth session and issues a new session id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
